- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply lagged mean reversion or cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75) after a peak, model should adjust downward by 1–3% per day until trend stabilizes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop — increase forecast decline rate or add 2–5% buffer below observed low.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently fails to capture late-cycle corrections — add 1–2% downward adjustment in final 5–7 days if sentiment turns negative or price shows divergence.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8 → 0.0 → 0.8), model should not assume linear trend — apply smoothing or weighted average of recent sentiment peaks and troughs.
